name: Rishikesh
description: Rishikesh sits at the foothills of the Himalayas where the Ganges exits the mountains, drawing a mix of yoga practitioners, white-water rafters, and Hindu pilgrims. The town splits between a commercialised southern stretch and the quieter, more atmospheric pedestrian zones around Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula. It suits active travellers and spiritual seekers well, but those expecting pristine mountain scenery should note the town itself is busy, littered in patches, and can feel chaotic in peak season.
nearest_railhead: Rishikesh Railway Station (last broad-gauge stop; 5 km from Ram Jhula) — Haridwar Junction (24 km) has far better connectivity
nearest_airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (DED) — approximately 35 km from Rishikesh town

attractions.name: Laxman Jhula
attractions.description: A narrow iron suspension bridge over the Ganges, historically significant and genuinely atmospheric, especially in early morning before crowds arrive. The bridge itself is modest; the real draw is the riverfront ghats, chai stalls, and temple alleyways on both banks.

attractions.name: Ram Jhula (Shivananda Jhula)
attractions.description: A wider suspension bridge than Laxman Jhula, flanked by large ashrams including Shivananda Ashram and Geeta Bhavan. The surrounding ghats are heavily used by pilgrims and offer good riverside access for an evening Ganga Aarti experience.

attractions.name: Triveni Ghat Evening Aarti
attractions.description: The main ritual bathing ghat in Rishikesh town where the largest evening Ganga Aarti is held daily after sunset. The ceremony is loud, colourful, and genuinely moving; arrive 30 minutes early to get a decent vantage point on the steps.

attractions.name: White-Water Rafting on the Ganges
attractions.description: Rishikesh is the most accessible white-water rafting base in India, with rapids graded II to IV depending on the stretch. The 16 km run from Shivpuri to Nim Beach is the most popular; the 36 km Marine Drive stretch offers more serious rapids and is only run October to April.

attractions.name: Riverside Camping at Shivpuri
attractions.description: A cluster of semi-permanent tented camps on Ganges riverbanks about 16 km upstream from Rishikesh, combining rafting day trips with campfire nights. Quality varies enormously between operators; the setting — forested hills, clear river — is genuinely good, but expect basic facilities.

attractions.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
attractions.description: A significant Shaivite temple at 1,330 m elevation, about 32 km from Rishikesh by road through dense forest. The drive or trek offers the best forest scenery near Rishikesh; the temple itself is heavily visited by pilgrims on weekends and can feel crowded. Weekday mornings are far more pleasant.

attractions.name: Rajaji National Park — Chilla Range Safari
attractions.description: The Chilla range of Rajaji Tiger Reserve lies roughly 10 km from Rishikesh and offers jeep safaris through sal forest with resident elephants, leopards, and occasionally tigers. Elephant sightings are fairly reliable in winter mornings; the park is closed June to mid-November.

attractions.name: Yoga & Meditation at Parmarth Niketan Ashram
attractions.description: Parmarth Niketan is the largest ashram in Rishikesh and one of the few that openly accepts walk-in visitors for daily yoga classes, meditation sessions, and the riverside evening aarti. It is less a tourist attraction than an immersive half-day or multi-day experience; quality of instruction is uneven.

attractions.name: Kunjapuri Devi Temple (Sunrise Viewpoint)
attractions.description: A hilltop Shakti temple at roughly 1,650 m, about 25 km north of Rishikesh, that offers one of the finest accessible Himalayan horizon views near the town — Bandarpoonch, Kedarnath range, and Chaukhamba visible on clear days. The pre-dawn drive up the forest road is part of the appeal; a genuine lesser-known alternative to the busy town ghats.

attractions.name: Phool Chatti to Laxman Jhula River Walk
attractions.description: A 7 km riverside trail from the small ashram village of Phool Chatti downstream to Laxman Jhula, largely unknown to package tourists. The path runs through forested riverbanks with good birding, solitary bathing spots, and no vendors — a genuine contrast to the busy town. A hidden gem that rewards early starters.
